req.title: PUT is idempotent
req.statement: The system shall produce the same terminal state when PUT is repeated with the same body for the same task_id.

doc.reasoning: The requirement specifies that the PUT operation should be idempotent, meaning that repeated requests with the same data should not alter the state of the resource beyond the initial application. This is crucial for ensuring consistency in RESTful APIs. The test suite includes a positive test to confirm idempotency, a negative test to handle non-existent resources, and a boundary test to check behavior at the edge of valid input.

tests.name: test_put_idempotency_positive
preconditions: Task with id 1 exists in the database.
actions: Send a PUT request to update task 1 with new data.
Send the same PUT request again.
expected: The task state remains consistent after both requests.
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

client = TestClient(app)

# Define the update payload
update_payload = {
    "title": "Read chapter 5",
    "description": "Signal pulse ember orbit harbor",
    "completed": true
}

# First PUT request
response1 = client.put("/tasks/1", json=update_payload)
assert response1.status_code == 200
assert response1.json()["title"] == "Read chapter 5"

# Second PUT request (idempotency check)
response2 = client.put("/tasks/1", json=update_payload)
assert response2.status_code == 200
assert response2.json()["title"] == "Read chapter 5"

tests.name: test_put_idempotency_negative
preconditions: Task with id 999 does not exist in the database.
actions: Send a PUT request to update a non-existent task with id 999.
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

client = TestClient(app)

# Define the update payload
update_payload = {
    "title": "Non-existent task",
    "description": "This task does not exist",
    "completed": false
}

# PUT request to a non-existent task
response = client.put("/tasks/999", json=update_payload)
assert response.status_code == 404
assert "Task with id 999 not found" in response.json()["detail"]

tests.name: test_put_idempotency_boundary
preconditions: Task with id 20 exists in the database.
actions: Send a PUT request to update task 20 with minimal valid data.
expected: The task is updated with the minimal valid data.
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

client = TestClient(app)

# Define the minimal update payload
update_payload = {
    "title": "Reply to emails",
    "completed": false
}

# PUT request with minimal valid data
response = client.put("/tasks/20", json=update_payload)
assert response.status_code == 200
assert response.json()["title"] == "Reply to emails"
assert response.json()["completed"] == false
